title: Collision Findings
description: IDEATE-stage artifact (novelty-collision-upgrade; see _design/novelty-collision-upgrade-LEDGER.md). The independent novelty-collision-checker worker's per-idea prior-art findings: it decomposes each idea into method×application×domain, emits targeted queries, runs real retrieval, and judges each near-hit. SEMANTIC-JUDGMENT-ONLY: this bundle records what the worker found and claims; it NEVER decides a cut. The deterministic gate (tools/novelty_collision.build_collision_verdict) decides — and a collision CUTS only on an existence-verified paper (citation_existence must pass), never on a vaguely-similar or unconfirmable one. A worker 'collision' whose papers fail existence becomes UNVERIFIED, never DEAD.

findings.description: One entry per idea the worker examined. Ideas with no entry are treated by the gate as CLEAR under grounded retrieval (no collision found, not proven novel).

method_combination.description: The decomposed method / technique combination under test (e.g. 'Tversky + boundary loss on a frozen foundation model').

application.description: The application / problem the idea targets (the 'on what' — e.g. 'inferior-alveolar-canal segmentation').

domain.description: The research domain / field the idea sits in (e.g. 'dental CBCT', 'NLP').

queries.description: The targeted retrieval queries the worker issued to hunt for prior art.

verdict.description: collision = a paper did this method×problem (gate fact-checks existence before any cut); adjacent = exists on a different application/problem or proposed-only (white space); clear = no collision found within coverage.

colliding_papers.description: The specific colliding papers (MUST be [] when verdict is 'clear'). Each must name a resolvable ref so the gate can existence-verify it; an unverifiable ref can never justify a cut.

ref.description: A resolvable citation: 'arXiv:2407.01517' | 'doi:10.xxxx/...' | a near-exact title. The gate runs citation_existence on this exact string.

does_same_method_on_same_problem.description: True only if this paper applies the SAME method combination to the SAME problem (not merely related). A DEAD cut requires True.

experimentally_validated.description: True if the paper actually RAN / implemented it (not merely proposed). When the gate's cut_requires_experiments is on, a DEAD cut requires True.

justification.description: Why this paper collides — the worker's reasoning.

quote.description: An optional verbatim snippet from the paper supporting the collision claim.

confidence.description: The worker's confidence in this finding (advisory; does not by itself decide the cut).

retrieval_note.description: Coverage / retrieval caveats (e.g. 'one source was unreachable; coverage partial').

evidence_ref.description: Pointer(s) to the worker's collision bundle (e.g. ['inbox/COLLISION.bundle.json']).
